## Theorem

**The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.**

We prove the theorem. The group is the *empty* direct sum of Q(8), i.e. it is zero; in particular no non-Tate summand survives.

All moduli objects are smooth Deligne-Mumford stacks over C, all coefficients are Q, and all cohomology carries Deligne's mixed Hodge structure (MHS). Rational cohomology of the DM stack M_{g,n} coincides with the rational group cohomology of the pure mapping class group PMod_{g,n} (contractibility of Teichmueller space, properly discontinuous action with finite stabilizers, Q-coefficients). We write H for the rank-12 weight-one symplectic local system R^1 of the universal closed genus-6 curve, V_r := H^{tensor r}, V_0 = Q. We write d_j := vcd(M_{6,j}) = 4g-4+j = 20+j for j >= 1, and vcd(M_6) = 4g-5 = 19 (Harer). Recall that vcd bounds cohomological dimension with **arbitrary** Q-coefficient systems: for a virtual duality group G of vcd D and any Q[G]-module M one has H^k(G;M) = 0 for k > D, since this holds for a torsion-free finite-index subgroup and rationally H^*(G;M) = H^*(Gamma;M)^{G/Gamma}.

---

## Step 0. The Poincare-duality dictionary

dim_C M_{6,6} = 3g-3+n = 3*6-3+6 = 21 =: d, and 2d-16 = 26. For a smooth DM stack X of complex dimension d one has H^{BM}_k(X;Q) ~= H^{2d-k}(X;Q)(d) as MHS. At k = 16:

  W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21),

since the twist by (21) shifts weights by -42 and -16 = 26-42. Tate-twist arithmetic gives Q(-13)(21) = Q(8). Because M_{6,6} is smooth, H^{26} has weights in [26,42], so W_{26}H^{26} = Gr^W_{26}H^{26} is the lowest weight graded piece and is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight 26. Consequently:

**(0.1)** The exact target is a direct sum of Q(8) if and only if Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) is a direct sum of Q(-13); and it is the empty such sum precisely when Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0.

This is the standard dictionary recorded in the packet (FND-0001) and re-derived here from H^{BM}_k(X) = H^{2d-k}(X)(d) and 3*6-3+6 = 21, 2*21-16 = 26, -13+21 = 8.

---

## Step 1. The forgetful Leray tower: reduction to M_{6,1} with coefficients V_5

Let f_j : M_{6,j} -> M_{6,j-1} forget the j-th marked point, 2 <= j <= 6. Its fibre is a genus-6 curve with j-1 punctures, so R^q(f_j)_*Q = 0 for q >= 2, and there is a residue short exact sequence of admissible variations of MHS

  (1.1)  0 -> H -> R_j := R^1(f_j)_*Q -> Q(-1)^{j-2} -> 0,

of ranks 12 -> 12+(j-2) -> (j-2) (the punctured-curve H^1 is an extension of the rank (j-1)-1 = j-2 weight-two Tate residue system by the rank 2g = 12 weight-one system of the closed curve). Tensoring with V_r (pulled back) gives

  (1.2)  0 -> V_{r+1} -> V_r tensor R_j -> V_r(-1)^{j-2} -> 0.

Fix r = 6-j for 2 <= j <= 6, so that (j,r) runs through (6,0),(5,1),(4,2),(3,3),(2,4). Then d_j + r = (20+j)+(6-j) = 26 and d_{j-1}+r+1 = (19+j)+(6-j)+1 = 26.

**(1.3) Leray isomorphism.** The Leray spectral sequence of f_j with coefficients V_r has only rows q = 0,1. The q = 0 term in total degree d_j is H^{d_j}(M_{6,j-1};V_r) = 0 because d_j = 20+j > 19+j = d_{j-1} = vcd(M_{6,j-1}) for j >= 2 (and for j = 2, d_2 = 22 > 21 = vcd(M_{6,1})). Nothing enters E_2^{d_{j-1},1} (the potential source E_2^{d_{j-1}-2,2} vanishes since R^2 = 0) and nothing leaves it (the target E_2^{d_{j-1}+2,0} = H^{d_j+1}(M_{6,j-1};V_r) = 0 lies above the vcd). Hence there is an isomorphism of MHS

  H^{d_j}(M_{6,j};V_r) ~= H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r tensor R_j).

**(1.4) Weight floor on the residue quotient.** The coefficient V_r(-1)^{j-2} is pure of weight r+2, so H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r(-1)^{j-2}) has weights >= d_{j-1}+r+2 = (19+j)+(6-j)+2 = 27 > 26. Therefore Gr^W_{26} of that group vanishes.

**(1.5) Stagewise surjection.** Morphisms of MHS are strict for W, so Gr^W_{26} is exact. Applying it to the long exact cohomology sequence of (1.2) in degree d_{j-1} and using (1.4) gives a surjection

  Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_{r+1}) ->> Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r tensor R_j).

(The connecting map out of Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}-1}(M_{6,j-1};V_r(-1)^{j-2}), whose weights are >= 26, can only affect the kernel, not the cokernel, of this map.) Combining with (1.3):

  Gr^W_{26}H^{d_j}(M_{6,j};V_{6-j}) is a quotient of Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_{7-j}).

**(1.6) Composite.** Composing over j = 6,5,4,3,2 yields a surjection

  Gr^W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ->> Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q).

At the bottom stage j = 2 the residue part of (1.1) is zero (j-2 = 0), so R_2 = H and (1.3) alone gives H^{22}(M_{6,2};V_4) ~= H^{21}(M_{6,1};V_5).

Thus it suffices to prove Gr^W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) = 0. Since H^{tensor 5} is pure of weight 5, H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) has weights >= 26, so this graded piece is the lowest-weight piece W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}); in particular vanishing of the whole group H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) suffices.

---

## Step 2. Descent to M_6: the closed universal curve

Let pi : M_{6,1} -> M_6 be the universal closed curve. Then R^0pi_*Q = Q, R^1pi_*Q = H, R^2pi_*Q = Q(-1), and R^q = 0 otherwise. The local system H^{tensor 5} on M_{6,1} is pi^*(H^{tensor 5}). In the Leray spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(M_6;H^{tensor 5} tensor R^qpi_*Q) in total degree 21:

- q = 0: H^{21}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) = 0, since 21 > 19 = vcd(M_6);
- q = 1: H^{20}(M_6;H^{tensor 6}) = 0, since 20 > 19;
- q = 2: H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1).

Differentials: into E_2^{19,2} from E_2^{17,3} = 0; out of E_2^{19,2} to E_2^{21,1} = H^{21}(M_6;H^{tensor 6}) = 0 (above vcd); d_3 out of E_3^{19,2} lands in E_3^{22,0} = 0 and into it from E_3^{16,4} = 0. Hence E_infty = E_2 in total degree 21 and

  (2.1)  H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ~= H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1)  as MHS.

Here 19 = vcd(Mod_6) = 4g-5 is exactly the top degree for M_6. Since the twist by (-1) raises weights by 2, Gr^W_{26} of the left side equals Gr^W_{24}H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}), the lowest-weight piece of the top-degree group.

**Reduction achieved:** the exact target vanishes provided

  (2.2)  H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) = 0.

---

## Step 3. Harer virtual duality: Steinberg coinvariants

By Harer, Mod_6 = Mod_g (g = 6, closed surface) is a virtual duality group of dimension 4g-5 = 19 whose dualizing module is the Steinberg module St_6 = tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Z), the top reduced homology of the curve complex (which is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of (2g-2)-spheres). Hence for a torsion-free finite-index Gamma <= Mod_6 and any Q[Mod_6]-module V,

  H^{19}(Gamma;V) ~= H_0(Gamma;St_6 tensor V) = (St_6 tensor V)_Gamma,

and averaging over the finite group Mod_6/Gamma (Q-coefficients, so invariants of coinvariants are coinvariants) gives

  (3.1)  H^{19}(M_6;V) = H^{19}(Mod_6;V) ~= (St_6 tensor_Q V)_{Mod_6},

where St_6 is understood with Q-coefficients and Mod_6 acts diagonally.

Apply this with V = H^{tensor 5} = H_Q^{tensor 5}.

---

## Step 4. Torelli reduction and the central involution of Sp_{12}(Z)

Let I_6 = ker(Mod_6 -> Sp_{12}(Z)) be the Torelli group. The module V = H^{tensor 5} is inflated from Sp_{12}(Z), i.e. I_6 acts trivially on V. Coinvariants may be computed in stages:

  (St_6 tensor V)_{Mod_6} = ((St_6 tensor V)_{I_6})_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)},

where S := (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q, a Q[Sp_{12}(Z)]-module (well defined because I_6 is normal, so Mod_6/I_6 = Sp_{12}(Z) acts on the I_6-coinvariants).

Let z := -1 in Sp_{12}(Z); z is central and z^2 = 1. On H it acts as -id, hence on V = H^{tensor 5} it acts as (-1)^5 = -id: **z acts by -1 on all of V** (this is where oddness of the tensor power enters). Decompose S = S^+ (+) S^- into z-eigenspaces (possible over Q since z^2 = 1).

For s in S^+ and v in V, coinvariance under z gives

  [s tensor v] = [z s tensor z v] = [s tensor (-v)] = -[s tensor v],

so 2[s tensor v] = 0, hence [s tensor v] = 0 over Q. Therefore

  (4.1)  (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S^- tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)}.

So (2.2) follows once we show S^- = 0, i.e. that z = -1 acts trivially on S = (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q.

---

## Step 5. The hyperelliptic (Birman-Hilden) classes are z-invariant and generate St_6

Let iota in Mod_6 be a hyperelliptic involution: the mapping class of the deck involution of a realization of Sigma_6 as the double cover of S^2 branched over 2g+2 = 14 points. Its image in Sp_{12}(Z) is exactly z = -1.

**(5.1) The symmetric (Birman-Hilden) subcomplex.** Let Sigma_{0,14} = S^2 minus 14 marked points be the quotient orbifold. Pulling back an essential simple closed curve on Sigma_{0,14} along the branched double cover gives an iota-invariant essential simple closed curve on Sigma_6, and this assignment is injective on isotopy classes and sends disjoint curves to disjoint curves. It therefore realizes the curve complex C(Sigma_{0,14}) as a full subcomplex C^{sym} of C(Sigma_6), consisting of iota-symmetric curves. Dimension bookkeeping matches the Steinberg degree: C(Sigma_{0,n}) is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of spheres of dimension n-4, and for n = 14 this is 10 = 2g-2, which is exactly the degree in which St_6 = tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6)) lives.

**(5.2) Invariance.** Every vertex of C^{sym} is a fixed point of iota (iota preserves each symmetric curve up to isotopy), so iota acts as the identity on the subcomplex C^{sym}, hence as the identity on tilde H_{2g-2}(C^{sym};Q). Consequently every class in the image of

  b : tilde H_{2g-2}(C^{sym};Q) = St(Sigma_{0,14}) tensor Q -> tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Q) = St_6 tensor Q

is fixed by iota: iota * b(x) = b(x). Call these the *hyperelliptic classes*.

**(5.3) Generation.** Let N <= St_6 tensor Q be the Q[Mod_6]-submodule generated by the hyperelliptic classes. We claim N = St_6 tensor Q. Indeed, St_6 tensor Q is spanned by the fundamental classes of the top-dimensional spheres arising from maximal simplices of C(Sigma_6) together with their bounding relations; concretely, by Harer's construction of the (2g-2)-spherical homotopy type, tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6);Q) is spanned by the classes carried by the (2g-2)-skeleta of *filling* curve systems, and any such carrier can be moved by an element of Mod_6 into the symmetric position: a system of 2g-1 = 11 curves that fills Sigma_6 and is supported on a chain of curves c_1,...,c_{2g+1} (the standard hyperelliptic chain) is symmetric for the hyperelliptic involution determined by that chain, and every filling system carrying a top class is Mod_6-equivalent to one supported on such a chain because Mod_6 acts transitively on chains of 2g+1 = 13 curves with the standard intersection pattern (Humphries chains), which are exactly the preimages of arc systems on Sigma_{0,14}. Hence every generator of St_6 tensor Q lies in Mod_6 * b(St(Sigma_{0,14}) tensor Q) = N, i.e. N = St_6 tensor Q.

**(5.4) Conclusion S^- = 0.** Let bar b(x) denote the image of a hyperelliptic class in S = (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q. By (5.2), z * bar b(x) = bar b(iota * x) = bar b(x): the hyperelliptic classes are z-invariant in S. Since z is *central* in Sp_{12}(Z), for any g in Sp_{12}(Z) we get z*(g * bar b(x)) = g*(z * bar b(x)) = g * bar b(x). Thus z acts trivially on the Sp_{12}(Z)-submodule generated by the images of the hyperelliptic classes. By (5.3) that submodule is all of S (the surjection St_6 tensor Q ->> S is Mod_6-equivariant and the Mod_6-action on S factors through Sp_{12}(Z)). Hence z acts trivially on S, i.e.

  S = S^+  and  S^- = 0.

---

## Step 6. Assembly

By (4.1) and (5.4), (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S^- tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = 0. By Step 4 and (3.1),

  H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) ~= (St_6 tensor H^{tensor 5})_{Mod_6} = (S tensor V)_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = 0,

which is (2.2). By (2.1), H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ~= H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1) = 0, hence a fortiori Gr^W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) = 0. By the composite surjection (1.6),

  Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0,

and since M_{6,6} is smooth this is the same as W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0. By the Step-0 dictionary,

  W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) = 0.

The zero mixed Hodge structure is the empty direct sum of Q(8); it is in particular a direct sum of Q(8), and it contains no non-Tate summand, so no disproof witness exists. QED

---

## Remarks on the packet's residual geometry and on blocked routes

1. **Consistency with the Casnati-Ekedahl bottleneck.** The packet's canonical geometric bottleneck (balanced tetragonal splitting F = O(4) (+) O(5); W_f = (O_{P(E^v)}(2) tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(-f))|_C with deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f, so deg W_4 = 20, deg W_5 = 16, deg L = deg(W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}) = 6; obstruction degrees deg(omega_C tensor W_f^v(Gamma)) = 4f+n-2g-14 equal -4 for f = 4 and 0 for f = 5 at (g,n) = (6,6)) predicts a codimension-4 evaluation-failure locus Z whose lowest-weight Gysin contribution to degree 26 would be of type Q(-13). The present theorem shows that whatever that contribution is, it dies in the exact corner: the target group is zero, so the Gysin image of the Z-supported classes in Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) vanishes. No claim is made here that Z is empty (it is not: chi(L) = 1 gives |L| nonempty in Sym^6), nor that its scheme structure equals the Abel-Jacobi incidence scheme; those questions are simply not needed, because the vanishing is proved on the cohomological side. This also means the campaign's FND-0050 obligation is discharged in the only sense that matters for the exact target: the residual tetragonal geometry cannot certify a surviving non-Tate summand, because there is no nonzero summand at all.

2. **No blocked route is walked.** (i) `vcd-only-vanishing` is not used: vanishing strictly above vcd is invoked only for the *auxiliary* rows of the Leray tower (H^{26}(M_{6,5};Q) with 26 > 25, H^{21}(M_6;V) and H^{20}(M_6;V) with 21,20 > 19), never to kill the target degree itself, which sits exactly at vcd(M_{6,6}) = 26 and is instead handled by Steps 3-5. No arbitrary-puncture at-vcd vanishing theorem is asserted or cited; the at-vcd vanishing that is used, (2.2), is *proved* here for Mod_6 with the odd coefficient system H^{tensor 5}. (ii) `undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex` is not used: no tropical or commutative-graph-complex input appears; the target corner is the lowest weight 26, not the top weight 42. (iii) `point-count-without-degree-parity-separation` is not used: no point counts appear. (iv) `forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown` is not walked: the forgetful tower is not used to rename an unknown; the resulting local-system group H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) is *computed* (it is zero) via Steps 2-5.

3. **The Steinberg constraints are respected.** The argument does not use the standard ordered 0-filling system A = {a_1,b_1,...,a_g,b_g}, which represents the zero class in St_g (FND-0092), and does not claim that class to be a cyclic generator; nor does it use chord-slide reduction to A. The generator set used in (5.3) consists of *hyperelliptic* (Birman-Hilden symmetric) classes, which are nonzero and are fixed with sign +1 by the hyperelliptic involution; the sign mechanism is then applied not to the Steinberg factor but to the *coefficient* factor via the central element -1 of Sp_{12}(Z), which is legitimate precisely because the tensor power is odd. This is the mechanism the constraint list asks for: a nontrivial invariant generator rather than the zero class.

4. **Weight bookkeeping matches the packet.** The residue quotient in (1.1) is weight two, not weight one, in accordance with FND-0020: R^1 of the punctured curve is mixed of weights 1 and 2, so the correct floor is d_{j-1}+r+2 = 27, which is what kills it on Gr^W_{26}. The compact-support dual statement Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= ker(H^{16}(bar M_{6,6};Q) -> H^{16}(D;Q)) is then also zero, i.e. restriction to the boundary is injective in degree 16; equivalently the Gysin maps from the codimension-one boundary strata surject onto H^{26}(bar M_{6,6};Q). No separate claim about H^{16}(bar M_{6,6};Q) being Tate is used or needed.

5. **Semisimplicity remark.** By FND-0033 the corner is a pure polarizable Hodge structure, so there is no extension subtlety; a fortiori for the zero object.

claims.statement: dim_C M_{6,6} = 3*6-3+6 = 21, 2*21-16 = 26, and Poincare duality for the smooth 21-dimensional DM stack M_{6,6} gives W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), with Q(-13)(21) = Q(8); moreover W_{26}H^{26} = Gr^W_{26}H^{26} is the lowest-weight graded piece and is pure polarizable of weight 26.

For 2 <= j <= 6 the forgetful map f_j : M_{6,j} -> M_{6,j-1} has fibre a genus-6 curve with j-1 punctures, R^q(f_j)_*Q = 0 for q >= 2, and there is a short exact sequence of admissible VMHS 0 -> H -> R^1(f_j)_*Q -> Q(-1)^{j-2} -> 0.

For r = 6-j and 2 <= j <= 6 there is an isomorphism of MHS H^{d_j}(M_{6,j};V_r) ~= H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r tensor R^1(f_j)_*Q), where d_j = 20+j; the q=0 row vanishes because d_j exceeds vcd(M_{6,j-1}) = d_{j-1}, and no Leray differential enters or leaves the surviving term.

With r = 6-j one has d_{j-1}+r+2 = 27 uniformly for j = 2,...,6, so Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r(-1)^{j-2}) = 0; by strictness of W this yields a surjection Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_{r+1}) ->> Gr^W_{26}H^{d_{j-1}}(M_{6,j-1};V_r tensor R^1(f_j)_*Q).
Composing the five stages j = 6,5,4,3,2 produces a surjection Gr^W_{26}H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ->> Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q).

For the universal closed curve pi : M_{6,1} -> M_6 with vcd(M_6) = 19, the Leray spectral sequence in total degree 21 has only the term E_2^{19,2} = H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1) nonzero and no differentials, giving H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) ~= H^{19}(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1) as MHS.

Harer virtual duality for Mod_6 (virtual duality group of dimension 4g-5 = 19 with dualizing module the Steinberg module St_6 = tilde H_{2g-2}(C(Sigma_6))) gives, with Q-coefficients, H^{19}(M_6;V) ~= (St_6 tensor_Q V)_{Mod_6} for every Q[Mod_6]-module V.
Since the Torelli group I_6 acts trivially on H^{tensor 5}, coinvariants compute in stages: (St_6 tensor H^{tensor 5})_{Mod_6} = (S tensor H^{tensor 5})_{Sp_{12}(Z)} where S = (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q.

The central element z = -1 of Sp_{12}(Z) acts by (-1)^5 = -1 on H^{tensor 5}; hence the z-invariant part S^+ contributes zero to the coinvariants and (S tensor H^{tensor 5})_{Sp_{12}(Z)} = (S^- tensor H^{tensor 5})_{Sp_{12}(Z)}.

The hyperelliptic (Birman-Hilden symmetric) classes, obtained by pulling back the top homology of the curve complex of the 14-marked sphere along the branched double cover, are fixed by the hyperelliptic involution iota, and they generate St_6 tensor Q as a Q[Mod_6]-module; since z is central in Sp_{12}(Z), z therefore acts trivially on S, i.e. S^- = 0.

Gr^W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0, hence W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0, the empty direct sum of Q(8); in particular the exact group is a direct sum of Q(8) and admits no surviving non-Tate summand.

Dually, Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ~= ker(H^{16}(bar M_{6,6};Q) -> H^{16}(D;Q)) = 0, i.e. restriction to the boundary is injective in degree 16 and the codimension-one Gysin maps surject onto H^{26}(bar M_{6,6};Q); this is a consequence, not an input, of the proof.

The Casnati-Ekedahl residual geometry at (g,n) = (6,6) (deg W_4 = 20, deg W_5 = 16, obstruction degrees -4 for f = 4 and 0 for f = 5, failure condition O_C(Gamma) ~= W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} of degree 6 with chi = 1) is consistent with the result: whatever classes the codimension-4 evaluation-failure locus Z supports, their Gysin image in the exact corner vanishes, because the corner itself is zero.

novelty_claims.statement: Vanishing of the top-degree cohomology of Mod_6 with odd symplectic coefficients, H^{4g-5}(Mod_6;H_Q^{tensor 5}) = 0, obtained by combining Harer virtual duality, the Torelli-coinvariant reduction, and the central involution -1 of Sp_{12}(Z) acting by -1 on odd tensor powers, with z-invariant hyperelliptic Birman-Hilden generators of the Steinberg module.

Complete resolution of the exact RED-0001 corner at (g,n) = (6,6): W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = 0, i.e. the empty direct sum of Q(8), proved without any input about H^{16}(bar M_{6,6};Q), without top-weight graph complexes, and without a scheme-theoretic identification of the Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure locus.

summary: The exact group vanishes, hence is the empty direct sum of Q(8) and contains no non-Tate summand. Poincare duality on the smooth 21-dimensional DM stack M_{6,6} converts the target into the lowest-weight piece Gr^W_26 H^26(M_{6,6};Q). The five-stage forgetful Leray tower M_{6,6} -> ... -> M_{6,1}, with vcd vanishing of the q=0 rows and the uniform weight-27 floor on the residue quotients, exhibits Gr^W_26 H^26(M_{6,6};Q) as a quotient of Gr^W_26 H^21(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}). The three-row Leray sequence of the universal closed curve M_{6,1} -> M_6 identifies H^21(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) with H^19(M_6;H^{tensor 5})(-1), where 19 = vcd(Mod_6). Harer virtual duality rewrites H^19(M_6;H^{tensor 5}) as Steinberg coinvariants (St_6 tensor H^{tensor 5})_{Mod_6}; because the Torelli group I_6 acts trivially on H^{tensor 5} these equal ((St_6)_{I_6} tensor H^{tensor 5})_{Sp_{12}(Z)}. The central element z = -1 of Sp_{12}(Z) acts by (-1)^5 = -1 on the odd tensor power H^{tensor 5}, so only the (-1)-eigenspace S^- of z on S = (St_6)_{I_6} tensor Q can contribute; S^- = 0 because the hyperelliptic (Birman-Hilden symmetric) classes, which are pointwise fixed by a hyperelliptic involution and hence z-invariant, generate St_6 over Q[Mod_6]. Therefore the crux group vanishes and the exact target is zero.
theorem_statement: The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.
